 Plus, experts share everything you need to get a Korean scalp facial at home without having to visit a salon or head spa. Oct. 29, 2026, 4:56 PM EDT Ashley Morris
 Associate SEO Reporter

 See 5 More Despite the name, facials aren’t limited to just your face; in fact, they can benefit your scalp, too. The Korean scalp facial is the latest in a long line of trending K-beauty routines, and for good reason: Those who’ve tried it rave about how it benefits their overall hair and scalp health . 
 To find out more about what a Korean scalp facial does, I spoke to Madeline June , a board-certified nurse practitioner specializing in cosmetic dermatology and aesthetic medicine at The Well Westlake , and Christina Kim, a board-certified esthetician and founder of dupï studio . I also compiled a list of expert- and NBC Selected editor-recommended cleansers, exfoliants, conditioners and treatments you can use to get one at home.

 What is a Korean scalp facial?
 A Korean scalp facial is basically a skin care-focused treatment for the scalp, according to my experts. “A Korean scalp facial applies the same principles used in Korean facial care, including gentle exfoliation, hydration, barrier support and massaging, but to the scalp,” says Kim. “This is often described as the ‘skinification’ of scalp care because the scalp is skin and deserves more than shampoo alone.”.
 Depending on the treatment, scalp facials can address issues like product buildup, excess oil, dry or flaky skin, congestion around the follicles and scalp irritation, says June. “It’s less about treating the hair shaft itself and more about caring for the skin underneath the hair,” she says. 
 However, despite its usefulness when addressing scalp and skin support, Kim warns against using Korean scalp facials as a substitute for medical treatment. “It’s not a medical treatment for hair loss, psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis or other scalp disorders,” she says. “Sudden shedding, painful inflammation, sores or persistent scaling should be evaluated by a dermatologist.”
 How to do the Korean scalp facial at home
 Below are the steps for a Korean scalp facial you’d get at a spa or hair salon, according to my experts. Although not all steps are necessary for an at-home treatment (for example, the scalp analysis step), you can still do most of these from the comfort of your home using the right products.
 Scalp analysis : During this step, the scalp is examined to look at oiliness, dryness, buildup, flaking or irritation and determine what type of treatment is appropriate, says June. (More on scalp facials and different scalp types below.)
 Pre-cleanse or oil treatment : Prior to cleansing, some treatments begin with a lightweight oil or scalp treatment to help loosen buildup and condition the scalp.
 Scalp cleansing: Use a gentle scalp shampoo (which are shampoos with ingredients targeted toward scalp health, like salicylic acid and rosemary extract) to remove oil, sweat and product buildup without stripping the scalp of its natural moisture.
 Exfoliation : Following the cleansing, a scalp exfoliant is used to gently remove dead skin cells and buildup around the hair follicles. “This step should be gentle, since aggressive scrubbing can irritate the scalp,” says June. Some common exfoliating ingredients include salicylic acid, tea tree oil and peppermint extract. 
 Scalp treatment or mask : Depending on your specific needs, you can use a hydrating, soothing or balancing treatment. For example, if you’re looking to hydrate a dry scalp, look for barrier-supporting ingredients like glycerin, panthenol, beta-glucan ceramides or urea, says Kim. 
 Scalp massage : Both June and Kim emphasize the importance of massaging your scalp, which helps distribute the products on your scalp. At her studio, Kim’s dry scalp facial focuses heavily on massage, which she says helps release tension around connected areas of the neck, shoulders, temples and scalp fascia, while also adding on lymphatic techniques and hitting acu-pressure points. “This prepares the client to relax and acknowledges that scalp tightness can be connected to tension held elsewhere,” she says.
 Rinse and conditioning : After the massage, thoroughly rinse the products from your hair and use a conditioner or deep conditioner as needed, says June.
 Final scalp or hair treatment : Finally, you can finish the treatment with a lightweight serum, tonic or leave-in product, which June says can help hydrate and soothe your scalp.
 How often should you do a scalp facial at home?
 How often you do a scalp treatment will depend on your scalp issues and what you use to treat them. However, June says that every four to six weeks is a reasonable amount for a healthy scalp. “At home, gentle cleansing can be part of your regular hair routine, while exfoliation should be much less frequent, often around once every one to two weeks if your scalp tolerates it,” she says. Kim agrees, and says that over-cleaning, over-exfoliation and excessive manipulation can actually result in worsening your scalp issues. “The best routine is one that keeps the scalp consistently comfortable, hydrated and balanced,” she says.
 Frequently asked questions 
 Which hair types would benefit most from a Korean scalp facial? Every hair type can benefit from a Korean scalp facial, experts say. But keep in mind, the products you use will vary depending on what your scalp concern is. 
 If you have an oily scalp , June suggests products that help clear buildup and exfoliate the scalp with ingredients like salicylic acid, glycolic acid and fruit enzymes and extracts.
 Those with dry or sensitive scalps may benefit more from gentle cleansing and hydration, says June. This includes products with moisture-friendly ingredients like panthenol, ceramides and exosomes.
 Textured/color-treated hair usually also needs products that help hold more moisture in the scalp and strands, says Kim. Look for humectants like glycerin, along with oils like jojoba and coconut oils to help seal in moisture.
 How does the Korean scalp facial differ from Western treatments? The biggest difference between Western and Korean hair treatments is in the focus on skin health. “Traditional Western hair treatments tend to focus more on the hair fiber itself, including things like repairing damage, adding moisture, reducing frizz or improving shine,” says June. Meanwhile, Korean philosophies on skin and scalp care are much more prevention-focused, says Kim. “Instead of aggressively stripping away every trace of oil, the intention is to cleanse thoroughly while preserving hydration and supporting the scalp barrier,” she says.
 How do lymphatic massages help your scalp? Lymphatic massages help to release tension through the connected areas of neck, shoulders, temples and scalp-fascia, which helps relieve tightness around the scalp, says Kim. The pressure should be gentle and controlled to prevent irritation. The massages can also help stimulate blood flow to your hair follicles and help hair grow, experts say.
